background: Modern distributed machine-learning clusters execute multiple training jobs simultaneously, where workers belonging to the same job must transmit large gradient tensors to their designated parameter server (PS) for global aggregation. In traditional architectures, this many-to-one traffic pattern creates significant network congestion and severe bandwidth bottlenecks at the PS. To mitigate this, programmable switches can be enabled with In-Network Aggregation (INA). By computing partial sums of gradients directly within the network fabric before the traffic reaches the PS, INA drastically reduces the total volume of bytes carried across the network. This technology effectively offloads the aggregation burden from the PS and alleviates the bandwidth saturation that typically limits cluster performance.
problem_requirement: Design and implement a scalable algorithm within the provided code template to solve the joint optimization problem of INA placement and traffic assignment, with the objective of minimizing the overall iteration makespan across all concurrently running jobs. The solution must navigate a complex set of physical and topological constraints: (1) INA deployment is limited by a strict switch budget $B_INA$; (2) each switch has a finite processing throughput limit; and (3) all network links have fixed bandwidth capacities. The algorithm must simultaneously decide which switches should host INA (placement) and assign each worker to a single optimal aggregation point (routing), adhering to practical rules such as “one chosen aggregation point per worker” and “at most one INA hop before the PS.” This involves explicitly modeling the coupling between placement and assignment—where poor placement causes hot spots and poor assignment underutilizes resources—while ensuring the final configuration satisfies all flow conservation, switch processing, and link bandwidth constraints defined in the underlying model.

problem_formulation.description: Joint optimization of In-Network Aggregation (INA) placement and worker-to-aggregator assignment to minimize training iteration makespan.

sets_and_parameters.J: Set of all concurrent distributed machine learning (DML) jobs.
sets_and_parameters.W_j: Set of workers belonging to job j.
sets_and_parameters.S: Set of candidate network switches available for INA deployment.
sets_and_parameters.d_j: The fixed Parameter Server (PS) node designated for job j.
sets_and_parameters.m_j: Gradient data volume per iteration for job j (e.g., in Gigabits).
sets_and_parameters.B_INA: Maximum budget for INA-enabled switches (Cardinality constraint).
sets_and_parameters.C_e^bw: Bandwidth capacity of physical link e (Gbps).
sets_and_parameters.C_s: Maximum processing throughput of switch s (Gbps) when INA is enabled.
sets_and_parameters.I_{u->v}(e): Binary parameter (Pre-calculated): 1 if link e is on the shortest path from node u to node v, 0 otherwise.
sets_and_parameters.M: Big-M constant: A sufficiently large number used to linearly model conditional constraints (e.g., if y=0, then rate=0).

decision_variables.x_s: Binary variable: 1 if switch s is selected to host INA, 0 otherwise.
decision_variables.y_{jwv}: Binary variable: 1 if worker w of job j is assigned to aggregation node v (where v can be an INA switch s or the PS d_j), 0 otherwise.

auxiliary_variables.alpha: Continuous variable representing the inverse of the makespan (1/t). Maximizing alpha minimizes the completion time.
auxiliary_variables.gamma_j: Continuous variable: The effective end-to-end throughput for job j, limited by the slowest component (straggler) in its aggregation tree.
auxiliary_variables.gamma_{jwv}: Continuous variable: The data transmission rate from worker w of job j to its assigned node v.
auxiliary_variables.gamma_{js}: Continuous variable: The aggregated data transmission rate from switch s to PS d_j for job j (exists only if switch s aggregates for job j).

objective.meaning: Maximize the reciprocal of the makespan. This is equivalent to minimizing the time t required for the slowest job to complete its gradient aggregation iteration.

constraints.name: Makespan Definition
constraints.expression: alpha <= gamma_j / m_j,  forall j in J
constraints.meaning: The global system speed alpha is constrained by the completion rate of every job. Specifically, alpha cannot exceed the inverse of any job's completion time.

constraints.name: Job Effective Rate (Straggler Logic)
constraints.expression: gamma_j <= sum(v in S U {d_j}) gamma_{jwv},  forall w in W_j, j in J
constraints.meaning: Job j's effective rate gamma_j is bottlenecked by its slowest worker. It cannot exceed the transmission rate of any individual worker w belonging to that job.

constraints.name: INA Placement Budget
constraints.meaning: The total number of switches enabled with INA capabilities must not exceed the hardware budget B_INA.

constraints.name: Single Aggregation Point Assignment
constraints.expression: sum(v in S U {d_j}) y_{jwv} = 1,  forall w in W_j, j in J
constraints.meaning: Each worker must send its gradient to exactly one destination: either an INA-enabled switch or directly to the PS.

constraints.name: Assignment Validity (INA Dependency)
constraints.expression: y_{jws} <= x_s,  forall w in W_j, s in S
constraints.meaning: A worker can only be assigned to switch s if switch s is actually selected to host INA (x_s = 1).

constraints.name: Rate-Assignment Coupling (Big-M)
constraints.expression: gamma_{jwv} <= M * y_{jwv},  forall w, j, v
constraints.meaning: If a worker is not assigned to node v (y=0), the flow rate on that link must be zero. If assigned, the rate is unbounded (up to M).

constraints.name: Switch Egress Flow Activation
constraints.expression: gamma_{js} <= M * sum(w in W_j) y_{jws},  forall s in S, j in J
constraints.meaning: An aggregated flow from switch s to PS d_j exists only if at least one worker from job j is assigned to switch s.

constraints.name: Aggregation Flow Consistency
constraints.expression: gamma_{js} >= gamma_j - M * (1 - sum(w in W_j) y_{jws}), forall s in S, j in J
constraints.meaning: If switch s is used by job j, the rate from s to PS must support the job's effective rate gamma_j. (Simplified flow conservation for aggregated traffic).

constraints.name: Switch Processing Capacity
constraints.expression: sum(j in J) sum(w in W_j) gamma_{jws} <= C_s * x_s,  forall s in S
constraints.meaning: The total volume of gradients arriving at switch s from all workers of all jobs must not exceed the switch's processing throughput C_s.

constraints.name: Physical Link Capacity
constraints.expression: Load_e(Worker->Switch) + Load_e(Worker->PS) + Load_e(Switch->PS) <= C_e^bw,  forall e
constraints.meaning: The sum of all traffic types traversing link e must not exceed the link's physical bandwidth. Loads are calculated by summing rates gamma where I_{u->v}(e) = 1.
